mechanism_narrative: Sustained positive WORKPLACES trend (t-1w: +1.1, t-0w: +1.4) signals workplace reopening momentum. This drives commuter retail visits during work-adjacent hours, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -2.0 to +1.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the prior 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM mobility (t-0w: +42.0, consistently >39%) reflects sustained essential-goods shopping behavior. Consumers making frequent essential trips exhibit higher incidental retail-and-recreation visits in the same shopping corridors, driving RETAIL_REC upward.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM sustained at 39.7–43.3 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase when GROCERY_PHARM remains above +35% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility stabilization (t-3w to t-0w: -3.4 to -0.7) combined with rising WORKPLACES (+1.4) indicates commuting infrastructure recovery. Restored transit capacity enables retail-district foot traffic, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks when both proxies move in tandem.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by >2 points week-on-week AND WORKPLACES remains positive
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improving, indicating decoupling of commuting recovery from retail visitation.

mechanism_narrative: Negative PARKS mobility (t-0w: -19.7) reflects outdoor-activity suppression, likely due to weather or restrictions. Suppressed outdoor recreation diverts leisure demand to indoor retail-and-recreation venues, producing a compensatory increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -19.7 in t-0w, -21.1 in t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase when PARKS is suppressed below -15%, or PARKS recovers without corresponding RETAIL_REC gains.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (t-0w: +4.4) combined with suppressed RETAIL_REC (t-0w: -1.9) indicates stay-at-home behavior or restrictions. If restrictions ease in the next four weeks, RESIDENTIAL will normalize and RETAIL_REC will rebound as consumers return to physical retail.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL elevated at 4.4–5.9 across four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above +4% while RETAIL_REC fails to increase, suggesting restrictions persist despite residential normalization signals.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of WORKPLACES recovery (+1.4), TRANSIT stabilization (-0.7), and sustained GROCERY_PHARM demand (+42.0) creates a multi-channel reopening signal. The joint presence of all three signals over two weeks triggers consumer confidence, driving RETAIL_REC upward as consumers perceive normalcy.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES > 0 AND TRANSIT improves by >1 point AND GROCERY_PHARM > 40 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:All three proxies show positive or stabilizing trends in t-0w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase despite simultaneous positive signals from WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and GROCERY_PHARM, indicating consumer confidence is not driven by these activity signals.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent RETAIL_REC suppression (t-3w to t-0w: -3.0 to -1.9) despite improving WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates structural retail weakness or consumer preference shift. Without a sharp reversal trigger, RETAIL_REC will remain depressed over the next four weeks, trending toward the baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC has remained negative across all four weeks, ranging from -3.4 to -1.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 points week-on-week in any of the next four weeks, indicating a structural break in the suppression pattern.

mechanism_narrative: Inverse relationship between PARKS suppression (-19.7) and RESIDENTIAL elevation (+4.4) indicates consumers are confined indoors. If PARKS remains suppressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, consumers lack outdoor alternatives and will not venture to retail-and-recreation venues, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -15% AND RESIDENTIAL remains above +4% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -19.7 and RESIDENTIAL at +4.4 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases despite sustained PARKS suppression and RESIDENTIAL elevation, indicating consumers are finding alternative retail pathways outside the home-confinement constraint.
